g.text: Persistent suffix graph — copy-on-write rebuild, log, then CAS-publish
(reads never block; acknowledged ⟹ durable AND visible)
an immutable `Arc` snapshot and traverse it lock-free.
Concurrent reads observe the committed snapshot — no writer lock
Step 1 — durability gate: append the Prepare record DURABLE, before any visibility
made visible before its op is durable.
Step 2 — rebuild the candidate off to the side (copy-on-write)
is private to this writer until the CAS publishes it.
Step 3 — publish: pointer-identity CAS (the linearization point)
published — NEW is now the live snapshot
[lost a race — another writer swapped first]
retry: reload root, rebuild on the newer base
The old snapshot is reclaimed once the last reader
holding its `Arc` drops it (reference-counted; no reader is ever interrupted).
On reopen the checkpoint image is loaded, then the durable
WAL tail is replayed: Prepare records whose matching Commit is durable are applied in
op_id order; un-committed Prepares are dropped. Recovery also folds the historical
length-prefixed monolithic WAL format when present.
